steps.intent: Open the reply composer for the opened email
Write an AI-authored reply based on the email's sender, subject and body into the Message Body (the recorded text is only an example)
Wait for the reply to auto-save as a draft ('Draft saved' notice)
Return to the inbox via 'Back to Inbox' to process the next unread email

dataFlow.field: sender name / subject / body of opened email (used to author reply)

successCriteria: The message view opens showing the email subject (h2.hP) after clicking an unread row
A Message Body textbox appears after clicking Reply
A 'Draft saved' notice appears after the reply text is entered
The Drafts count (#dcount) increases by one per processed email
No Send button is ever clicked; the email is not sent
consequentialActions: Send email (the Send button appears in the reply composer) — the widget must NEVER press Send; it only leaves replies as auto-saved drafts

strategyHints.reason: Opening an email is a client-side click on an inbox row; no network calls observed
Reply link click reveals the composer in the DOM; no network calls
Text must be inserted into a contenteditable textbox with input events so auto-save fires
Draft saving is observable only via the live 'Draft saved' toast and #dcount; no network request recorded
Navigation back is a DOM button (aria-label 'Back to Inbox')

openQuestions: Should the widget draft replies for all unread emails or only the currently open / newest N?
What tone, length, or sign-off should the AI-written replies use?
Should emails that already have a saved draft be skipped?
